name: DeepSeek-V2.5

lifecycle.note: Weights are still public and ungated on Hugging Face. In the DeepSeek API, deepseek-chat moved to DeepSeek-V2.5-1210 on 2024-12-10.

replacedBy.note: In the DeepSeek API only: deepseek-chat was upgraded to DeepSeek-V2.5-1210. The weights stay available.

relations.note: DeepSeek merged DeepSeek-V2-0628 with DeepSeek-Coder-V2-0724 (code line, not a record in Model History). The model card names the parents more loosely as DeepSeek-V2-Chat and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct.

summary.text: DeepSeek-V2.5 is a language model that DeepSeek made by merging DeepSeek-V2-0628 with its code model DeepSeek-Coder-V2-0724, to combine general conversation and coding in one model. It was released on 2024-09-05 in DeepSeek's web chat and API, where it served both deepseek-chat and deepseek-coder, and as open weights under the DeepSeek Model License.

changes.text: Merges the general chat model DeepSeek-V2-0628 with the code model DeepSeek-Coder-V2-0724 into one model.
One model now serves both the deepseek-chat and deepseek-coder API models, which DeepSeek kept for backward compatibility.
DeepSeek says it defined safety boundaries more clearly, making the model more resistant to jailbreaks while applying safety policies to normal requests less often.
DeepSeek says the model aligns better with human preferences and improves writing and instruction following.

features.note: In the DeepSeek API; DeepSeek says Function Calling, FIM completion and JSON output remain unchanged.

openWeights.note: DeepSeek Model License (license link in the model card).

notes: Served through both API ids deepseek-chat and deepseek-coder for backward compatibility; neither id is used as an alias because both served other models over time. The DeepSeek-V2.5 name aliases are candidate because the December 2024 revision DeepSeek-V2.5-1210 is also called DeepSeek-V2.5. The model card refers to the DeepSeek-V2 page for model details, so parameters and context window are not restated here. Category code not added: DeepSeek presents it as combining general and coding abilities, not as a code-first model.
